newsitem.title: UK: EU seen hard-pressed to export higher sugar output.
newsitem.headline: EU seen hard-pressed to export higher sugar output.

text.p: The European Union (EU) could face difficulties disposing of its expected larger sugar output into 1997 as export outlets and traditional homes start to dry up, German statistician F.O. Licht said on Wednesday.
In its second estimate of European beet sugar production for 1996/97, Licht said the EU should produce 17.40 million tonnes of sugar in raw value terms, 392,000 tonnes higher than 1995/96.

"With white sugar in plentiful supply, particularly in view of the fact that the new refineries in the Middle East will be operating, there may be problems in disposing of the higher crop expected in the EU, especially as there is expected to be a fall in demand for white sugar," Licht said.
It added that the EU was likely to carry over more sugar from the current crop than had been originally anticipated, which could in turn lead to lower beet sowings in 1997.
"Protectionist measures by the Russian government may lead to reduced imports from the Ukraine and that, too, could lead to lower sowings," it said.

In order to protect its domestic industry, Russia has imposed a white sugar import quota of 1.5 million tonnes with a limit of 1.15 million tonnes from the Ukraine, thus limiting the amount of EU sugar which could theoretically be imported.
"There would appear to be little opportunity for high quality EU white sugar to find much of an outlet in Russia," Licht said in its report.
